### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e199adfb79ba2eddb79ad7d5fb0e827c6fb653c1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cdc2ebcafcc9d6ce63cfc059f76818392ba42128` — the merge of head `fbe1de197eabf684e6437116d4ba555af2de1413` into base `e199adfb79ba2eddb79ad7d5fb0e827c6fb653c1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cdc2ebcafcc9d6ce63cfc059f76818392ba42128 && git checkout cdc2ebcafcc9d6ce63cfc059f76818392ba42128
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e199adfb79ba2eddb79ad7d5fb0e827c6fb653c1 fbe1de197eabf684e6437116d4ba555af2de1413 && git checkout -B drift-repro e199adfb79ba2eddb79ad7d5fb0e827c6fb653c1 && git merge --no-ff fbe1de197eabf684e6437116d4ba555af2de1413

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e199adfb79ba2eddb79ad7d5fb0e827c6fb653c1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e199adfb79ba2eddb79ad7d5fb0e827c6fb653c1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Seat ACCEPT · PR #28014 · head `fbe1de197eabf684e6437116d4ba555af2de1413` · 2026-10-30T08:20Z

## 维护者速读

A declarative connector that was unreachable at boot sits degraded and retries on a backoff. Before this change, if a retry later reached the upstream and the provider refused the instance's configuration (for example an `include` naming a tool the MCP server does not list), the instance stayed on the retry timer with the stale "could not reach" reason. Now that retry ends it: the instance is held with the configuration reason, and only an edit of its declaration or a restart re-attempts it, as ADR-0097 says for configuration faults. A refused credential keeps its hold path, and an unreachable upstream keeps retrying.

## 席位核对

- **Shape:** draft → main, `Fixes #27992`, 3 files: `plugin.ts` (+50, one new branch in the reconcile catch and one helper), a new test file, and a changeset (`@objectstack/service-automation` patch).
  - `check-governed-merges --pr 28014`: NOT governed, +292 / −0.
- **Read of the diff:** the new branch runs only when the call is not fatal (not boot) and the instance is already degraded. It sets the existing `held` flag with the configuration reason. It re-registers the husk with that reason unless a previously materialised connector is still serving, and logs once at `error`, with the provider's message in `meta` per #5575. The boot-time and reload-time paths for an instance that is not degraded are untouched.
- **Deviation the seat accepted:** triage 6516917595 says "into the failed state". `ConnectorState` has only `ready` and `degraded`, so the dev reused the existing `held` mark. Every observable part of the graded rule holds: the reason is replaced, the retry stops, and an edit or a restart re-attempts. No new state was added to a published type.
- **Tests:** 6 cases. `mcp` and `openapi` each take the configuration reason and are not retried across 64× the base delay. An unchanged reload does not re-attempt, and an edit recovers to `ready`. A live connector pending a changed entry keeps serving and stops retrying. Controls: unreachable keeps retrying, and a refused credential stays held. The card thread reports 4 of 6 red on `main`, an ablation that reds 4 with the controls green, and a clean restore.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch. No published face narrows, so no contract review is owed.
- **Skills-docs / follow-up:** the PR body says "follow-up owed" (`content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`). That row is carried by #28016, together with a dispatch refusal that still tells a held instance "the platform retries automatically" (`connector-nodes.ts:76`, which needs engine knowledge of the hold, so it is not in this PR).
- **Local (card thread):** package suite 2836/2836, typecheck green, 60 of 60 derived gate families exit 0, `pnpm lint` green.
- **Gate check-runs on this head:** 48 total, 35 success, 13 skipped by the path filter, 0 failed. `mergeable_state: clean`.
- **Landing:** Tier S, under the maintainer's landing grant for this term (2026-10-29 22:05Z, seat thread). Ready + auto-merge through the relay.

**ACCEPT**
